This separation prevents a legal-provenance correction from silently expanding into a geopolitical evidence migration.


## Verified corrections


### 1. Iranian maritime sources


The source split remains valid:


- `SRC-IRAN-MARINE-ACT-1993` — Iranian municipal statute reproduced by UN DOALOS.
- `SRC-US-DOS-LIS-114-1994` — attributed U.S. Department of State legal analysis.


The phrase beginning **“Many of these claims do not comport…”** belongs to *Limits in the Seas No. 114*, not to Iran’s Act and not to a UN legal determination.


### 2. IRGC oil-reporting date


The Reuters article is dated **December 18, 2024**, not December 2023.


Use:


```
source_id: SRC-REUTERS-IRGC-OIL-2024-12-18publication_date: 2024-12-18
```


Do not use:


```
source_id: SRC-REUTERS-2023-12-IRGC-OILpublication_date: 2023-12
```


### 3. Oil-discount claim


The supplied material should not collapse the discount reporting into one undifferentiated `$1–8` range. Decompose it:


```
claim_id: CLAIM-IRGC-OIL-DISCOUNT-TYPICAL-001claim_text: >  Reuters reported that an involved source described the IRGC discount  relative to NICO prices as typically $1–2 per barrel.epistemic_status: SOURCE_ASSERTIONattribution_form: ALLEGED_BY_SOURCEsource_id: SRC-REUTERS-IRGC-OIL-2024-12-18
```


```
claim_id: CLAIM-IRGC-OIL-DISCOUNT-UPPER-001claim_text: >  Reuters reported that the discount could reach as much as $8 per barrel  in some circumstances.epistemic_status: SOURCE_ASSERTIONattribution_form: ALLEGED_BY_SOURCEsource_id: SRC-REUTERS-IRGC-OIL-2024-12-18
```


These are attributed reporting, not independently verified market measurements.


### 4. “Up to 50%” claim


Normalize the claim without converting the Reuters headline into a fact:


```
claim_id: CLAIM-IRGC-OIL-SHARE-001claim_text: >  Reuters reported that six specialists estimated that the IRGC controlled  up to 50% of Iranian oil exports, compared with approximately 20% three  years earlier; Reuters stated that it could not independently determine  the exact extent of that control.claim_type: SOURCE_ASSERTIONclaim_status: UNVERIFIEDepistemic_status: SOURCE_ASSERTIONattribution_form: ALLEGED_BY_SOURCEsource_id: SRC-REUTERS-IRGC-OIL-2024-12-18source_locator: article-body-estimates-and-methodology
```


The corresponding graph node must be claim-centric:


```
CLAIM-IRGC-OIL-SHARE-001
```


Not:


```
IRGC_Oil_Export_Control
```


The latter silently encodes the disputed assertion as a graph fact.

## Corrected AmSC friction assessment


The submitted friction note contains useful analytical hypotheses but overstates what cryptographic and graph systems can establish.


| Submitted statement | Corrected registration |
| --- | --- |
| AmSC “freezes reality” into hashes | AmSC can canonicalize and hash a captured digital representation; it does not freeze or prove external reality |
| Proof Tree makes lineage “unalterable” | An append-only, access-controlled graph can make unauthorized changes detectable; this requires demonstrated implementation and audit controls |
| History cannot be “scrubbed or spoofed” | Post-ingest alteration may be detectable, but upstream source spoofing, omission, sensor deception, and compromised ingestion remain possible |
| AmSC “interdicts the flow” | AmSC maps and analyzes reported relationships; operational interdiction is outside scope |
| `4D Lattice Advantage` | Source-supplied analytical framing, not a validated performance advantage |


Register the corrected assessment as:


```
assessment_id: ASSESS-AMSC-IRGC-FRICTION-001assessment_type: ANALYTICAL_INFERENCEepistemic_status: ANALYTICAL_INFERENCEclaim_status: UNVERIFIEDsource_id: SRC-USER-PDF-AMSC-IRGC-FRICTION-001allowed_for_orientation: trueallowed_for_automated_action: falsecryptographic_execution_status: PENDINGgraph_integrity_validation: NOT_EXECUTEDhuman_review_required: true
```


Recommended wording:


> AmSC can preserve the integrity and transformation history of captured digital objects through canonicalization, digests, append-only records, and review controls. These mechanisms do not prove that source observations are true, complete, independently corroborated, or immune to pre-ingest deception.

## Architecture adoption matrix


| Paper concept | LIBERTAS adoption | Qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two-pass contract compilation | Adopt | Completeness pass followed by ambiguity and scope pass |
| Persistent Markdown memory | Adopt | Permanent records require human approval; rolling observations remain mutable |
| Role-specialized agents | Adopt | Roles do not imply independent evidence |
| Independence-based verification | Adopt with caveat | Structural separation reduces shared implementation blindness but does not prove model independence |
| Attention-based verification | Adopt | Different review roles inspect different surfaces |
| Four-way failure arbiter | Adopt | Add `BUG`, `SPEC_GAP`, `NOISE`, and `CONTRACT_AMBIGUITY` |
| Outer-loop calibration | Adopt | Proposed memory and contract changes require review |
| Early deployment metrics | Reference only | Author-reported and not a LIBERTAS performance baseline |

Fetch un-indexed features, claims, and sources    const { results: features } = await env.DB.prepare(      `SELECT feature_id, name, feature_class, layer_id, epistemic_status FROM geo_features WHERE navigation_suitability = 0`    ).all();    const { results: claims } = await env.DB.prepare(      `SELECT claim_id, claim_text, epistemic_status, claim_type FROM claims`    ).all();    const { results: sources } = await env.DB.prepare(      `SELECT source_id, title, source_class FROM evidence_sources WHERE review_state != 'Superseded'`    ).all();    const vectorsToUpsert: VectorizeVector[] = [];    // 2. GeoFeatures    for (const f of features as any[]) {      const text = `Feature: ${f.name} | Class: ${f.feature_class} | Layer: ${f.layer_id} | Status: ${f.epistemic_status}`;      const emb = await env.AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', { text: [text] });      vectorsToUpsert.push({        id: f.feature_id,        values: emb.data[0],        metadata: { type: 'GeoFeature', name: f.name, layer_id: f.layer_id, epistemic_status: f.epistemic_status }      });    }    // 3. Sources (provenance chunks)    for (const s of sources as any[]) {      const text = `Source: ${s.title} | Class: ${s.source_class} | ID: ${s.source_id}`;      const emb = await env.AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', { text: [text] });      vectorsToUpsert.push({        id: s.source_id,        values: emb.data[0],        metadata: { type: 'Source', source_class: s.source_class }      });    }    // 5. Batch upsert (edge)    if (vectorsToUpsert.length > 0) {      await env.VECTORIZE.upsert(vectorsToUpsert);    }    return Response.json({      status: 'SUCCESS_DRY_RUN',      indexed_count: vectorsToUpsert.length,      notice: 'GraphRAG semantic vector space seeded. ### I. THE TRIPTYCH OF INSTRUMENTS — STRATEGIC INTELLIGENCE VIEW


> ***The IRGC is represented as a vertically integrated intelligence-operations organism whose influence is better mapped as corridors, flows, and network relationships than as fixed territory.***


The cartography model has four major layers:


1. **Triptych command layer**
2. **Proxy-network geometry**
3. **African corridor subgraph**
4. **American Science Cloud / Libertas verification layer**


The doctrinal outcome is:## Agent Roles – [[Proposer_Agent]] – [[Critic_Agent]] – [[Policy_Agent]] – [[Security_Agent]] – [[Provenance_Agent]] – [[Cost_Latency_Agent]] – [[Human_Review_Agent]] – [[Consensus_Engine]] ## Maritime Corridor – [[Maritime_Corridor_Map]] – [[Strait_of_Hormuz_Theater_Layer]] – [[Red_Sea_Theater_Layer]] – [[Maritime_Domain_Awareness]]


> ***Map flows, not footprints. Verify evidence, not assumptions. Track provenance, not rhetoric.***

### 1. Quds Force — External Covert Operations & Proxy Management


The Quds Force is responsible for **foreign clandestine activity**, including support to proxy groups that have been responsible for severe harm and destabilization in multiple regions. From an intelligence‑mapping perspective, the Quds Force forms the **outer operational ring** of the IRGC system:


- External covert operations
- Proxy force coordination
- Arms movement and covert logistics
- Influence operations abroad


This is the **expeditionary vector** of the Intel Spine.


### 2. Basij — Internal Stabilization & Mass Mobilization


The Basij functions as the **domestic enforcement and mobilization layer**, enabling the regime to maintain internal control. In intelligence cartography, the Basij is the **ground mesh**:


- Internal security enforcement
- Rapid mobilization
- Ideological conditioning
- Domestic suppression


It stabilizes the home front so external operations can continue uninterrupted.


### 3. IRGC Intelligence Branches — Targeting, Geospatial Intelligence, Covert Networks


These branches form the **analytic and reconnaissance core** of the IRGC system:


- Target development
- Geospatial and operational intelligence
- Covert network construction
- Counterintelligence and internal vetting


This is the **brainstem** of the Intel Spine — the layer that identifies corridors, chokepoints, and exploitable seams.


## II. THE INTEL SPINE — THE BACKBONE OF IRGC GLOBAL OPERATIONS


The three instruments above interlock into a **single intelligence architecture**:


### Quds Force → External vector


### Basij → Internal stabilizer


### IRGC Intelligence → Targeting & coordination


Together, they form the **Intel Spine**, a vertically integrated intelligence‑operations system that blends:


- Ideology
- Logistics
- Covert action
- Influence networks
- Cyber infrastructure


This is why the IRGC behaves like a **state‑within‑a‑state**, as the uploaded study notes:


> “The IRGC has become extremely powerful described as ‘a state‑within‑a‑state’.”


## III. PROXY NETWORK GEOMETRY — MULTI‑DOMAIN INFLUENCE LATTICE


This is where the IRGC’s intelligence architecture becomes **cartography** — a map of influence corridors rather than borders.


### 1. Arms Flows (Unit 190)


Unit 190 has been linked to covert arms transfers into conflict zones. From an intelligence‑layer perspective, this is the **material logistics vector**.


### 2. Ideological Propagation


Religious, cultural, and educational outreach programs create **soft‑power corridors** that precede or accompany proxy development.


### 3. Maritime Logistics Claude_Fable_5_ACT_Reasoning_Controller


![](https://media.licdn.com/dms/image/v2/D4E12AQHQtmp1ABkQlA/article-inline_image-shrink_1000_1488/B4EZ9Rq825JIAI-/0/1783781643846?e=1786579200&v=beta&t=6VXN6Udq-IOooEgqR_7i85_Hs0l926cqnPHmhPWazvI)


Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, and Mediterranean routes form **maritime ingress pathways** that connect Africa, the Middle East, and beyond.


### 4. Cyber Infrastructure (APT35 / Charming Kitten / Moses Staff)


These cyber clusters operate as **digital corridors**, mirroring the physical ones:


- Credential harvesting
- Influence operations
- Infrastructure procurement
- Psychological operations


APT35 and Moses Staff have been associated with Iranian state‑linked cyber activity by multiple governments and security researchers, and their operations have caused harm through espionage and information theft.


## IV. WHY THIS IS A MULTI‑DOMAIN INFLUENCE LATTICE


The IRGC does **not** operate in isolated silos. It operates as a **lattice** — a cross‑domain mesh where:


- Cyber supports logistics
- Logistics supports proxies
- Proxies support ideology
- Ideology supports recruitment
- Recruitment supports covert operations


This is why the IRGC’s influence map looks like a **graph**, not a region.


The uploaded study reinforces this:


> “Africa is the perfect battlefield for Iran’s expansionist project.”


The IRGC uses **geography as infrastructure**, not territory.


## V. CIA‑STYLE INTELLIGENCE SUMMARY (HIGH‑ALTITUDE)


### Assessment


The IRGC’s Triptych forms a **vertically integrated intelligence‑operations system** that blends internal control, external projection, and covert networks into a unified architecture.


### Implications


- Proxy networks are **multi‑domain**, not single‑discipline.
- Influence corridors operate across **physical, ideological, financial, and cyber** layers.
- The Intel Spine is the **coordinating mechanism** that binds these domains.


### Strategic Understanding


To map IRGC activity, one must map **corridors**, not borders — **flows**, not footprints.

[https://www.linkedin.com/company/office-of-the-under-secretary-for-science-and-innovation/posts/](https://www.linkedin.com/company/office-of-the-under-secretary-for-science-and-innovation/posts/)One of the most exciting aspects of the Genesis Mission is the growing community behind it.

Today, at the inaugural Genesis Mission Summit, we announced more than $800 million in committed partner support through the Genesis Mission Consortium. These contributions, announced alongside our first Genesis Mission research awards, represent another important step in building a national platform for AI-enabled scientific discovery.

These commitments go beyond funding. Consortium members are contributing advanced AI models, compute resources, cloud infrastructure, scientific expertise, research partnerships, and other capabilities that will help researchers move faster and tackle some of our nation’s most ambitious scientific challenges.

From the beginning, the Genesis Mission was designed to bring together the strengths of [**U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)**](https://www.linkedin.com/company/energy/)‘s National Laboratories, industry, academia, and other partners. No single institution can build the future of science alone. By combining our capabilities, we can accelerate discovery, strengthen our energy leadership, and advance our national security.

## RAG Query Trace Simulation


### Overview


The task involves simulating a full Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) query trace through the knowledge graph structure. The query is: “How does the IRGC’s role in securing Iranian oil exports intersect with U.S. efforts to counter foreign political interference tied to China’s energy dependencies?”


### Step 1: Query Ingestion and Embedding


1. **Input**: User submits the query.
2. **Action**: Pipeline embeds the query, semantically matching key vectors: “IRGC oil security”, “China energy dependency”, “U.S. counterstrategy”.
3. **Top Nodes/Sources Activated**:
  - IRGC_Oil_Security
  - China_Energy_Dependency
  - US_IndoPacific_Response


### Step 2: Graph Traversal


1. **Start at Node**: IRGC_Oil_Security
  - Recall: IRGC protects oil routes/facilities, secures revenue stream—especially for China.
  - Timestamp: 2025-04-15
  - Geo: Strait of Hormuz, Persian Gulf
  - Attributes: Maritime, asymmetric deterrence, dual-alignment chokepoint.
2. **Edge Traverse**:
  - IRGC_Oil_Security — [enables_energy_flow/0.82] → China_Energy_Dependency
3. **Node**: China_Energy_Dependency
  - Recall: China needs steady Iranian oil to support Belt & Road industrial nodes and economic growth.
  - Timestamp: 2025-04-01
  - Attributes: High dependency, risk tolerance (sanctions circumvention), non-Western bloc.
4. **Edge Traverse**:
  - China_Energy_Dependency — [complicates_policy/0.91] → US_IndoPacific_Response
5. **Node**: US_IndoPacific_Response
  - Recall: U.S. must balance deterrence, sanctions, and diplomacy across multiple theaters; constrained by China-Iran coordination.
  - Timestamp: 2025-06-01
  - Geo: Indo-Pacific, South China Sea
  - Attributes: Strategic balancing, simultaneous deterrence constraints.
6. **Additional Edge**:
  - IRGC_Oil_Security — [provokes_counterstrategy/0.88] → US_IndoPacific_Response


### Step 3: Timeline and Escalation Layer Cross-ref


1. **Relevant Timeline Tags**:
  - 2025-04-15: IRGC Oil Convoy Protection (energy security milestone)
  - 2025-06-01: U.S. Indo-Pacific Response (strategic counter)
2. **Escalation Links Activated**:
  - “Doctrinal revenge” (2020 Soleimani Strike → 2024 IRGC directive)
  - “Strategic persistence” (2024 IRGC directive → 2025 energy security)


### Step 4: Dashboard/Heatmap Overlay


1. **Risk Layer Triggered**:
  - Volatility flagged over the Strait of Hormuz, Chinese supply nodes, and U.S. naval presence.
2. **Escalation Effect**:
  - Chokepoint/seaborne risk peaks, diplomatic flexibility declines (tradeoff value: 0.74).


### Step 5: RAG Output Structured Summary


```
{  "answer": "The IRGC's robust control over Iranian oil exports—especially to China—creates an economic lifeline that underpins both Iranian state revenues and regional proxy operations. Batch upsert (edge)    if (vectorsToUpsert.length > 0) {      await env.VECTORIZE.upsert(vectorsToUpsert);    }    return Response.json({      status: 'SUCCESS_DRY_RUN',      indexed_count: vectorsToUpsert.length,      notice: 'GraphRAG semantic vector space seeded. AI Overview


The ‘Act on the Marine Areas of the Islamic Republic of Iran’ (1993) is Iran’s primary domestic legislation establishing its territorial sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone, and continental shelf. It defines its territorial waters as 12 nautical miles and requires foreign warships to obtain prior permission before passing through. [[1](https://2009-2017.state.gov/documents/organization/58228.pdf), [2](https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/ira1666.pdf), [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz)]


While Iran helped negotiate the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), it never ratified the treaty. Therefore, its maritime claims are governed by this 1993 domestic act, causing certain points of friction with international norms: [[1](https://tehranbureau.com/hormuz/), [2](https://2009-2017.state.gov/documents/organization/58228.pdf)]


1. The Territorial Sea and Right of Passage


Under standard international law (UNCLOS), foreign military and commercial ships have a right of “innocent passage” through another country’s territorial waters without needing prior permission. The 1993 Iranian law breaks from this norm by requiring foreign warships, submarines, and nuclear-powered vessels to notify or get permission prior to passing through. [[1](https://www.facebook.com/Qnewsegy/posts/is-irans-declared-controlled-maritime-zone-in-strait-of-hormuz-legally-valid-und/122284698494134472/), [2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz)]


2. The Strait of Hormuz


Because of its unique geography and global reliance on the shipping lanes, the Strait of Hormuz acts as an international strait. UNCLOS provides a “transit passage” right for international navigation, which is harder for coastal nations to block or restrict. Since Iran is not a party to UNCLOS, it does not recognize this specific right, leading to ongoing disputes with the United States and other naval powers over navigation rights. [[1](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/news/2026/04/no-ordinary-stretch-sea-who-governs-the-strait-of-hormuz), [2](https://e-arc.ro/en/2026/05/02/the-strait-of-hormuz-crisis-a-legal-perspective-2/), [3](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=El16eW7pZ1M&t=43), [4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz)]


3. Economic and Security Zones


The 1993 Act claims an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) extending up to 200 nautical miles from its baseline. Within this zone, Iran’s laws prohibit foreign military activities and practices that they deem inconsistent with their rights and national interests. [[1](https://stjececmsdusgva001.blob.core.usgovcloudapi.net/public/documents/Iran2023.pdf), [2](https://tehranbureau.com/hormuz/), [3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strait_of_Hormuz)]


You can read the full, official English text in the [United Nations DOALOS Document](https://www.un.org/depts/los/LEGISLATIONANDTREATIES/PDFFILES/IRN_1993_Act.pdf). [[1](https://academic.oup.com/edited-volume/42608/chapter/357548924), [2](https://2009-2017.state.gov/documents/organization/58228.pdf)]

### II. Vectorize Embedding Seed Script (scripts/seed_vectorize.ts)


This worker utility embeds conceptual theater features and claims (such as `CLAIM-IRGC-CORRIDOR-MODEL-001`) into the Cloudflare `Vectorize` index for GraphRAG semantic neighbor search (`/v1/orient`):


TypeScript


```
import { Ai } from '@cloudflare/ai';export interface Env {  AI: Ai;  VECTORIZE: VectorizeIndex;  DB: D1Database;}export default {  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {    // 1. Fetch un-indexed spatial features & claims from D1    const { results: features } = await env.DB.prepare(      `SELECT feature_id, name, feature_class, layer_id FROM geo_features`    ).all();    const { results: claims } = await env.DB.prepare(      `SELECT claim_id, claim_text, epistemic_status FROM claims`    ).all();    const vectorsToUpsert: VectorizeVector[] = [];    // 2. Generate embeddings for GeoFeatures    for (const f of features as any[]) {      const text = `Feature: ${f.name} | Class: ${f.feature_class} | Layer: ${f.layer_id}`;      const emb = await env.AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', { text });            vectorsToUpsert.push({        id: f.feature_id,        values: emb.data[0],        metadata: { type: 'GeoFeature', name: f.name, layer_id: f.layer_id }      });    }    // 3. Generate embeddings for Source Claims    for (const c of claims as any[]) {      const text = `Claim: ${c.claim_text} | Epistemic Status: ${c.epistemic_status}`;      const emb = await env.AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', { text });      vectorsToUpsert.push({        id: c.claim_id,        values: emb.data[0],        metadata: { type: 'Claim', epistemic_status: c.epistemic_status }      });    }    // 4. Batch upsert into Vectorize Edge Index    if (vectorsToUpsert.length > 0) {      await env.VECTORIZE.upsert(vectorsToUpsert);    }    return Response.json({      status: 'SUCCESS',      indexed_count: vectorsToUpsert.length,      notice: 'GraphRAG semantic vector space seeded successfully at the edge.'    });  }};
```

**Human review:** Required


## Deterministic validation findings


1. Actor-related statements are stored as **claims**, not geographic facts.
2. `CONTROLS`, `TARGETS`, `COMMANDS`, `DIRECTS`, `OWNS`, `OPERATES_IN`, and `RESPONSIBLE_FOR` remain prohibited edge relationships.
3. “Iranian control on the north shore” is normalized to **Iranian territorial-sea jurisdiction adjacent to its coast**. It must not become an IRGC-control edge.
4. `epistemic_status: UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION → PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED` cannot be stored as one field. Use:
  - `epistemic_status: UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION`
  - `proposed_epistemic_status: PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED`
  - an approved transition record before promotion.
5. `claim_status: SOURCE_ASSERTION` mixes two fields. Correct representation:
  - `claim_type: SOURCE_ASSERTION`
  - `claim_status: UNVERIFIED`
6. Source material supports a general finding of Iranian and IRGC-QF material assistance and training to the Houthis. It does **not automatically verify** every asserted city-level presence, route, sensor relay, or command relationship.
7. Claims about Sanaa, Saada, Hodeidah, Dhofar, direct IRGC coordination, and specific staging functions require individual source locators.
8. GeoJSON coordinates remain `[longitude, latitude]` and are non-navigational.

> This migration avoids subqueries inside SQLite `CHECK` constraints. SQLite does not permit subqueries in `CHECK` expressions.


```
PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Authoritative source registry-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS evidence_sources (    source_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,    title TEXT NOT NULL,    publisher TEXT,    source_url TEXT,    source_class TEXT NOT NULL        CHECK (            source_class IN (                'USER_SUPPLIED_PARSED_TEXT',                'PRIMARY_OFFICIAL',                'INTERGOVERNMENTAL',                'SECONDARY_REPORTING',                'ANALYTICAL_RESEARCH'            )        ),    publication_date TEXT,    source_reliability TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Unassessed',    information_credibility TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Unassessed',    file_sha256 TEXT,    review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',    created_at TEXT NOT NULL        DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')));-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Locations may exist without geometry. This prevents invented coordinates.-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS location_references (    location_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,    name TEXT NOT NULL,    location_class TEXT NOT NULL        CHECK (            location_class IN (                'city',                'port',                'maritime-region',                'chokepoint',                'coastal-region',                'administrative-region'            )        ),    parent_region TEXT,    longitude REAL        CHECK (longitude IS NULL OR longitude BETWEEN -180.0 AND 180.0),    latitude REAL        CHECK (latitude IS NULL OR latitude BETWEEN -90.0 AND 90.0),    geometry_basis TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING'        CHECK ( 'REVIEWED_ASSESSMENT',                'VERIFIED_FACT',                'REJECTED',                'SUPERSEDED'            )        ),    attribution_form TEXT NOT NULL        CHECK ( 'LEGAL_GEOGRAPHIC_REFERENCE',                'UNRESOLVED'            )        ),    source_id TEXT NOT NULL,    source_locator TEXT NOT NULL,    source_supplied_confidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Unknown'        CHECK (            source_supplied_confidence IN (                'Unknown',                'Low',                'Low-Moderate',                'Moderate',                'Moderate-High',                'High'            )        ),    assessment_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'NOT_ADJUDICATED',    allowed_for_orientation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,    allowed_for_automated_action INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0        CHECK (allowed_for_automated_action = 0),    human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1        CHECK (human_review_required = 1),    review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',    created_at TEXT NOT NULL        DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),    FOREIGN KEY (source_id)        REFERENCES evidence_sources(source_id));-- A location link expresses geographic relevance, never actor control.CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claim_location_links (    link_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,    claim_id TEXT NOT NULL,    location_id TEXT NOT NULL,    relationship TEXT NOT NULL        CHECK (            relationship IN (                'RELATED_TO',                'LOCATED_IN',                'OBSERVED_AT',                'REFERENCES'            )        ),    evidence_ids_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'        CHECK (json_valid(evidence_ids_json)),    review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',    FOREIGN KEY (claim_id)        REFERENCES corridor_claims(claim_id),    FOREIGN KEY (location_id)        REFERENCES location_references(location_id));-- Evidence may support, contradict, or contextualize a claim.CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claim_evidence_links (    link_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,    claim_id TEXT NOT NULL,    source_id TEXT NOT NULL,    source_locator TEXT NOT NULL,       'INDEPENDENT',                'PARTIALLY_DEPENDENT',                'DEPENDENT',                'UNKNOWN'            )        ),    review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',    FOREIGN KEY (claim_id)        REFERENCES corridor_claims(claim_id),    FOREIGN KEY (source_id)        REFERENCES evidence_sources(source_id));-- Additional defense in depth.CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS ## Deploying Location Intelligence using Cloudflare Serverless Architecture


### Overview


The task involves deploying the Location Intelligence layer onto Cloudflare’s serverless architecture. This includes incorporating the [[Red_Sea_Theater_Layer]], [[Strait_of_Hormuz_Theater_Layer]], and [[GeoJSON_Spatial_Fabric]].


### Cloudflare Serverless Architecture


The architecture utilizes Cloudflare Pages/Workers, D1 (Serverless SQL Database), Workers KV (ultra-fast GeoJSON cache), and Vectorize (GraphRAG latent expansion).


1. **CLOUDFLARE WRANGLER CONFIGURATION (wrangler.jsonc)**:
  - Configure serverless bindings for D1, KV Namespace, and Vectorize.


```
{  "$schema": "node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",  "name": "libertas-location-intelligence",  "main": "src/index.ts",  "compatibility_date": "2026-07-01",  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],  "d1_databases": [    {      "binding": "DB",      "database_name": "libertas_spatial_fabric",      "database_id": "YOUR_D1_DATABASE_ID"    }  ],  "kv_namespaces": [    {      "binding": "THEATER_CACHE",      "id": "YOUR_KV_NAMESPACE_ID"    }  ],  "vectorize": [    {      "binding": "VECTORIZE",      "index_name": "libertas-theater-embeddings"    }  ],  "vars": {    "FRAMEWORK": "LIBERTAS_v6.10",    "LOCATION_CONTROLLER": "Claude_Fable_5",    "EXECUTION_MODE": "DRY_RUN"  }}
```


1. **D1 GEOSPATIAL DATABASE MIGRATION (migrations/0001_spatial_schema.sql)**:
  - Define the schema for storing spatial features and relational nodes.


```
CREATE TABLE geo_features (  feature_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  layer_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES theater_layers(layer_id),  name TEXT NOT NULL,  feature_class TEXT NOT NULL,  geometry_type TEXT NOT NULL,  geometry_json TEXT NOT NULL,  min_lon REAL NOT NULL,  min_lat REAL NOT NULL,  max_lon REAL NOT NULL,  max_lat REAL NOT NULL,  navigation_suitability INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION');CREATE INDEX idx_features_bbox ON geo_features(min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat);
```


### Implementation


1. **Provision Edge Stores**:
  - Create D1 database, KV namespace, and Vectorize index.
2. **Apply Spatial Schema**:
  - Apply the spatial schema to the D1 database.
3. **Deploy**:
  - Deploy the application using Wrangler.

The Obsidian knowledge vault structure remains as previously defined:


```
LIBERTAS_LATTICE_V6/├── 00_INDEX/├── 01_DOCTRINE/├── 02_GRAPH/├── 03_OODA/├── 04_LOCATION_INTELLIGENCE/│   ├── Red_Sea_Theater_Layer.md│   ├── Strait_of_Hormuz_Theater_Layer.md│   ├── GeoJSON_Spatial_Fabric.json├── 05_PROVENANCE/├── 07_DECISION_MAPPING/├── 08_EVIDENCE_CHAINS/├── 09_POLICY/├── architecture.md├── README.md└── package.json
```

1. **`Red_Sea_Theater_Layer.md`** and **`Strait_of_Hormuz_Theater_Layer.md`**:
  - Represent maritime domain awareness for the respective regions.
2. **`GeoJSON_Spatial_Fabric.json`**:
  - Contains GeoJSON data for the regions.
3. **`Location_Intelligence_Cloudflare_Deployment.md`**:
  - Documents the Cloudflare edge deployment.


By following this structured approach, the Location Intelligence layer is effectively deployed onto Cloudflare’s serverless architecture, ensuring a scalable and performant solution for spatial intelligence.

function canonicalize(value: unknown): string {  // RFC 8785 (JCS) subset: recursive key sort, no whitespace.  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') return JSON.stringify(value)  if (Array.isArray(value)) return '[' + value.map(canonicalize).join(',') + ']'  const obj = value as Record<string, unknown>  const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort()  return '{' + keys.map(k => JSON.stringify(k) + ':' + canonicalize(obj[k])).join(',') + '}'}async function sha256Hex(input: string): Promise<string> {  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(input))  return [...new Uint8Array(buf)].map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')}
```


validateObservation: required fields per admission contract: observation_id, source_id, source_locator, timestamp, claim_status default UNVERIFIED, epistemic_status must be in controlled list and MUST NOT be VERIFIED_FACT at ingestion (silent-upgrade guard!). That’s a nice touch: ingestion rejects epistemic_status in {‘VERIFIED_FACT’,’REVIEWED_ASSESSMENT’,’CORROBORATED’} without transition_id + human_review_id.


Envelope helper:


```
function envelope(c: any, data: unknown, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {  return {    data,    provenance: {      framework: c.env.FRAMEWORK,      generated_at: new Date().toISOString(),      epistemic_notice: 'All records are claims pending lineage and review.',      navigation_suitability: false,      classification: c.env.CLASSIFICATION,      ...extra    }  }}
```


rowToFeature:


```
function rowToFeature(row: any) {  return {    type: 'Feature',    id: row.feature_id,    properties: {      feature_id: row.feature_id,      layer_id: row.layer_id,      name: row.name,      feature_class: row.feature_class,      epistemic_status: row.epistemic_status,      claim_status: row.claim_status,      confidence: row.confidence,      attribution_form: row.attribution_form,      source_id: row.source_id,      source_locator: row.source_locator,      review_state: row.review_state,      human_review_required: !!row.human_review_required,      canonical_digest: row.canonical_digest,      navigation_suitability: false,      operational_use: 'PROHIBITED'    },    geometry: JSON.parse(row.geometry_json)  }}
```

On May 2, 1993, the Government of Iran completed legislative action on an “Act on the
Marine Areas of the Islamic Republic of Iran in the Persian Gulf and the Oman Sea.” On
July 6, 1993, the Iran notified the Secretary General of the United Nations of the legislation.1
The legislation provides a reasonably comprehensive set of maritime claims to a territorial
sea, contiguous zone, exclusive economic zone (EEZ), and continental shelf, and Iran’s
jurisdictional claims within those areas. Many of these claims do not comport with the
requirements of international law as reflected in the 1982 United Nations Convention on the
Law of the Sea (LOS Convention). The Act replaces provisions of earlier Iranian
legislation:

**2. D1 Geospatial Migration**


— LIBERTAS_v6.10 Spatial Fabric — D1/SQLite


— Invariants: coordinate order [longitude, latitude]; navigation_suitability always 0;


— every claim-bearing row carries epistemic_status; promotions require transition records.


PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;


CREATE TABLE epistemic_ranks (


status TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


rank INTEGER NOT NULL


);


INSERT INTO epistemic_ranks VALUES


(‘UNKNOWN’, 0), (‘SOURCE_ASSERTION’, 1), (‘UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION’, 1),


(‘CONTESTED’, 2), (‘ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE’, 2), (‘PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED’, 3),


(‘CORROBORATED’, 4), (‘REVIEWED_ASSESSMENT’, 5), (‘VERIFIED_FACT’, 6),


(‘REJECTED’, 0), (‘SUPERSEDED’, 0), (‘REFERENCE_METADATA’, 0);


CREATE TABLE theater_layers (


layer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


name TEXT NOT NULL,


region TEXT NOT NULL,


description TEXT,


navigation_suitability INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (navigation_suitability = 0),


epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘REFERENCE_METADATA’


CHECK (epistemic_status IN (SELECT status FROM epistemic_ranks)),


review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘Pending’


CHECK (review_state IN (‘Pending’,’InReview’,’Approved’,’ApprovedWithConditions’,’Returned’,’Rejected’)),


human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,


created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(‘%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ’,’now’))


);


CREATE TABLE geo_features (


feature_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


layer_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES theater_layers(layer_id),


name TEXT NOT NULL,


feature_class TEXT NOT NULL


CHECK (feature_class IN (‘chokepoint’,’port-facility’,’subsea-cable’,’corridor’,


‘historical-incident’,’energy-transit’,’commercial-traffic’,’reference’)),


geometry_type TEXT NOT NULL


CHECK (geometry_type IN (‘Point’,’LineString’,’Polygon’,’MultiPoint’,’MultiLineString’,’MultiPolygon’)),


geometry_json TEXT NOT NULL, — GeoJSON geometry; coordinates [lon, lat]


min_lon REAL NOT NULL, min_lat REAL NOT NULL,


max_lon REAL NOT NULL, max_lat REAL NOT NULL,


coordinate_order TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘LON_LAT’ CHECK (coordinate_order = ‘LON_LAT’),


navigation_suitability INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (navigation_suitability = 0),


epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION’


CHECK (epistemic_status IN (SELECT status FROM epistemic_ranks)),


claim_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘UNVERIFIED’,


confidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘Unknown’


CHECK (confidence IN (‘Unknown’,’Low’,’Moderate’,’High’,’Verified’)),


attribution_form TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘UNRESOLVED’


CHECK (attribution_form IN (‘DIRECT_SOURCE_STATEMENT’,’ALLEGED_BY_SOURCE’,


‘ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE’,’SPATIAL_ASSOCIATION_ONLY’,’UNRESOLVED’)),


source_id TEXT, source_locator TEXT,


review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘Pending’,


human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,


canonical_digest TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘PENDING’,


created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(‘%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ’,’now’))


);


CREATE INDEX idx_features_bbox ON geo_features(min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat);


CREATE INDEX idx_features_layer ON geo_features(layer_id);


CREATE TABLE observations (


observation_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


feature_id TEXT REFERENCES geo_features(feature_id),


source_id TEXT NOT NULL,


source_locator TEXT NOT NULL,


observed_at TEXT NOT NULL,


ingested_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(‘%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ’,’now’)),


epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION’


CHECK (epistemic_status IN (SELECT status FROM epistemic_ranks)),


claim_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘UNVERIFIED’,


attribution_form TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘UNRESOLVED’,


canonical_digest TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘PENDING’,


review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘Pending’,


human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1


);


— AEQUITAS deterministic verification: block silent epistemic promotion.


CREATE TRIGGER trg_no_silent_upgrade


BEFORE UPDATE OF epistemic_status ON observations


FOR EACH ROW


WHEN (SELECT rank FROM epistemic_ranks WHERE status = NEW.epistemic_status)


> (SELECT rank FROM epistemic_ranks WHERE status = OLD.epistemic_status)


AND NOT EXISTS (


SELECT 1 FROM epistemic_transitions t


WHERE t.object_id = OLD.observation_id


AND t.old_epistemic_status = OLD.epistemic_status


AND t.new_epistemic_status = NEW.epistemic_status


AND t.final_disposition IN (‘APPROVE’,’APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS’))


BEGIN


SELECT RAISE(ABORT, ‘AEQUITAS_BLOCK: epistemic promotion requires approved transition record’);


END;


CREATE TABLE epistemic_transitions (


transition_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


object_id TEXT NOT NULL,


old_epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL,


new_epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL,


transition_reason TEXT NOT NULL,


transition_evidence_ids TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘[]’,


old_digest TEXT NOT NULL, new_digest TEXT NOT NULL,


human_review_id TEXT NOT NULL,


final_disposition TEXT NOT NULL


CHECK (final_disposition IN (‘APPROVE’,’APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS’,’RETURN’,’REJECT’,’DEFER’)),


created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(‘%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ’,’now’))


);


CREATE TABLE claims (


claim_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


claim_text TEXT NOT NULL,


epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘SOURCE_ASSERTION’


CHECK (epistemic_status IN (SELECT status FROM epistemic_ranks)),


attribution_form TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘ALLEGED_BY_SOURCE’,


source_id TEXT, source_locator TEXT,


assessment_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘NOT_ADJUDICATED’,


allowed_for_orientation INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,


allowed_for_automated_action INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (allowed_for_automated_action = 0),


human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1


);


CREATE TABLE evidence_chain_links (


link_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,


chain_id TEXT NOT NULL,


from_node TEXT NOT NULL,


to_node TEXT NOT NULL,


relationship TEXT NOT NULL


— AEQUITAS: actor-control edges cannot be auto-created at the edge layer.


CHECK (relationship NOT IN (‘CONTROLS’,’DIRECTS’,’OWNS’,’OPERATES_IN’,


‘RESPONSIBLE_FOR’,’TARGETS’,’COMMANDS’)),


evidence_ids TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ‘[]’,


created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime(‘%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ’,’now’))


);

**3. src/index.ts — Hono Edge Router**


import { Hono } from ‘hono’


import { secureHeaders } from ‘hono/secure-headers’


type Bindings = {


DB: D1Database


THEATER_CACHE: KVNamespace


VECTORIZE: VectorizeIndex


AI: Ai


FRAMEWORK: string


DOCTRINE: string


LOCATION_CONTROLLER: string


EXECUTION_MODE: ‘DRY_RUN’ | ‘LIVE’


CLASSIFICATION: string


}


const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }>()


app.use(‘*’, secureHeaders())


// ── VERITAS provenance envelope on every response ─────────────────────────


app.use(‘*’, async (c, next) => {


await next()


c.header(‘X-Libertas-Framework’, c.env.FRAMEWORK)


c.header(‘X-Libertas-Execution-Mode’, c.env.EXECUTION_MODE)


c.header(‘X-Libertas-Navigation-Suitability’, ‘false’)


c.header(‘X-Libertas-Epistemic-Axiom’, ‘Reports are claims requiring lineage’)


})


// ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


const canonicalize = (v: unknown): string => {


// RFC 8785 (JCS) subset: recursive key sort, no whitespace. Conformance PENDING.


if (v === null || typeof v !== ‘object’) return JSON.stringify(v)


if (Array.isArray(v)) return ‘[‘ + v.map(canonicalize).join(‘,’) + ‘]’


const o = v as Record<string, unknown>


return ‘{‘ + Object.keys(o).sort()


.map(k => JSON.stringify(k) + ‘:’ + canonicalize(o[k])).join(‘,’) + ‘}’


}


const sha256Hex = async (s: string): Promise<string> => {


const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest(‘SHA-256’, new TextEncoder().encode(s))


return […new Uint8Array(buf)].map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, ‘0’)).join(”)


}


const envelope = (c: any, data: unknown, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => ({


data,


provenance: {


framework: c.env.FRAMEWORK,


generated_at: new Date().toISOString(),


navigation_suitability: false,


classification: c.env.CLASSIFICATION,


notices: [


‘Conceptual OSINT analytical rendering — not a navigational product.’,


‘GeoJSON coordinate order is [longitude, latitude].’,


‘Spatial proximity is not actor attribution.’,


‘Retrieval rank is not evidence strength.’,


],


…extra,


},


})


const rowToFeature = (r: any) => ({


type: ‘Feature’,


id: r.feature_id,


properties: {


feature_id: r.feature_id, layer_id: r.layer_id, name: r.name,


feature_class: r.feature_class, epistemic_status: r.epistemic_status,


claim_status: r.claim_status, confidence: r.confidence,


attribution_form: r.attribution_form, source_id: r.source_id,


source_locator: r.source_locator, review_state: r.review_state,


human_review_required: !!r.human_review_required,


canonical_digest: r.canonical_digest,


navigation_suitability: false, operational_use: ‘PROHIBITED’,


},


geometry: JSON.parse(r.geometry_json),


})


// ── Health ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


app.get(‘/health’, (c) => c.json(envelope(c, {


status: ‘CONTEXT_OPERATIONAL’,


controller: c.env.LOCATION_CONTROLLER,


doctrine: c.env.DOCTRINE,


execution_mode: c.env.EXECUTION_MODE,


})))


// ── Layer registry (KV-cached) ─────────────────────────────────────────────


app.get(‘/v1/layers’, async (c) => {


const key = ‘idx:layers:v1’


const hit = await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.get(key, ‘json’)


if (hit) return c.json(envelope(c, hit, { cache: ‘HIT’ }))


const { results } = await c.env.DB.prepare(


`SELECT layer_id, name, region, description, epistemic_status, review_state


FROM theater_layers ORDER BY layer_id`).all()


await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.put(key, JSON.stringify(results), { expirationTtl: 60 })


return c.json(envelope(c, results, { cache: ‘MISS’ }))


})


// ── Theater layer as GeoJSON FeatureCollection (KV-cached) ────────────────


app.get(‘/v1/layers/:layerId/geojson’, async (c) => {


const layerId = c.req.param(‘layerId’)


const key = `layer:${layerId}:geojson:v1`


const hit = await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.get(key)


if (hit) return c.json(JSON.parse(hit))


const { results } = await c.env.DB.prepare(


`SELECT * FROM geo_features WHERE layer_id = ?1`).bind(layerId).all()


if (!results.length)


return c.json({ error: ‘LAYER_NOT_FOUND’, layer_id: layerId }, 404)


const fc = {


type: ‘FeatureCollection’,


name: layerId,


metadata: {


framework: c.env.FRAMEWORK, doctrine: c.env.DOCTRINE,


coordinate_order: ‘[longitude, latitude]’,


navigation_suitability: false,


generated_at: new Date().toISOString(),


},


features: results.map(rowToFeature),


}


await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.put(key, JSON.stringify(fc), { expirationTtl: 30 })


return c.json(fc)


})


// ── Bounding-box spatial query (indexed) ──────────────────────────────────


app.get(‘/v1/spatial/bbox’, async (c) => {


const q = c.req.query()


const nums = [‘min_lon’, ‘min_lat’, ‘max_lon’, ‘max_lat’].map(k => Number(q[k]))


if (nums.some(Number.isNaN)) return c.json({ error: ‘INVALID_BBOX’ }, 400)


const [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] = nums


if (minLon < -180 || maxLon > 180 || minLat < -90 || maxLat > 90)


return c.json({ error: ‘BBOX_OUT_OF_RANGE’ }, 400)


const { results } = await c.env.DB.prepare(


`SELECT * FROM geo_features


WHERE max_lon >= ?1 AND min_lon <= ?3 AND max_lat >= ?2 AND min_lat <= ?4`)


.bind(minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat).all()


return c.json(envelope(c, {


type: ‘FeatureCollection’, features: results.map(rowToFeature),


}, { query_bbox: [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] }))


})


// ── ORIENT — GraphRAG semantic neighbor search (Vectorize + Workers AI) ────


app.get(‘/v1/orient’, async (c) => {


const q = c.req.query(‘q’)


if (!q) return c.json({ error: ‘QUERY_REQUIRED’ }, 400)


const emb = await c.env.AI.run(‘@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5’, { text: q })


const matches = await c.env.VECTORIZE.query(emb.data[0], {


topK: 5, returnMetadata: ‘all’,


})


return c.json(envelope(c, {


query: q,


semantic_neighbors: matches.matches.map(m => ({


id: m.id, score: m.score, metadata: m.metadata ?? {},


})),


doctrinal_rule: ‘The language model may explain the graph. It must not replace the graph.’,


edge_policy: ‘Only explicit D1 relationships are returned. No inferred edges.’,


}))


})


// ── OBSERVE — provenance-gated ingestion (DRY_RUN default) ────────────────


app.post(‘/v1/observe’, async (c) => {


const intent = c.req.header(‘X-Validated-Intent’) // ACT admission contract


const body = await c.req.json().catch(() => null) as any


if (!body?.observation_id || !body?.source_id || !body?.source_locator || !body?.observed_at)


return c.json({ error: ‘ADMISSION_FAILURE’,


missing: [‘observation_id’, ‘source_id’, ‘source_locator’, ‘observed_at’]


.filter(k => !body?.[k]) }, 422)


// AEQUITAS silent-upgrade guard at the API edge


const requested = body.epistemic_status ?? ‘UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION’


const blockedAtIngest = [‘VERIFIED_FACT’, ‘REVIEWED_ASSESSMENT’, ‘CORROBORATED’]


if (blockedAtIngest.includes(requested) && !body.transition_id)


return c.json({ error: ‘AEQUITAS_BLOCK’,


detail: ‘Elevated epistemic_status at ingestion requires approved transition_id.’ }, 403)


const record = {


…body,


epistemic_status: requested,


claim_status: body.claim_status ?? ‘UNVERIFIED’,


review_state: ‘Pending’,


human_review_required: true,


}


const digest = await sha256Hex(canonicalize(record))


const live = c.env.EXECUTION_MODE === ‘LIVE’ && intent && body.human_review_id


if (!live) {


return c.json(envelope(c, {


dry_run: true,


admission: intent ? ‘INTENT_PRESENT_BUT_NOT_LIVE’ : ‘NO_INTENT_DRY_RUN’,


would_insert: { …record, canonical_digest: `sha256:${digest}` },


}), 202)


}


await c.env.DB.prepare(


`INSERT INTO observations


(observation_id, feature_id, source_id, source_locator, observed_at,


epistemic_status, claim_status, canonical_digest)


VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5, ?6, ?7, ?8)`)


.bind(record.observation_id, body.feature_id ?? null, record.source_id,


record.source_locator, record.observed_at, record.epistemic_status,


record.claim_status, `sha256:${digest}`).run()


return c.json(envelope(c, { inserted: record.observation_id,


canonical_digest: `sha256:${digest}` }), 201)


})


// ── Provenance walk ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


app.get(‘/v1/provenance/:observationId’, async (c) => {


const id = c.req.param(‘observationId’)


const obs = await c.env.DB.prepare(


`SELECT * FROM observations WHERE observation_id = ?1`).bind(id).first()


if (!obs) return c.json({ error: ‘OBSERVATION_NOT_FOUND’ }, 404)


const { results: links } = await c.env.DB.prepare(


`SELECT * FROM evidence_chain_links WHERE from_node = ?1 OR to_node = ?1`)


.bind(id).all()


return c.json(envelope(c, { observation: obs, explicit_edges: links }))


})


export default app


---


**4. Deployment Sequence**


# 1 — Provision edge stores


npx wrangler d1 create libertas_spatial_fabric


npx wrangler kv namespace create THEATER_CACHE


npx wrangler vectorize create libertas-theater-embeddings –dimensions=768 –metric=cosine


# 2 — Apply spatial schema (layers, AEQUITAS trigger, conceptual seed features)


npx wrangler d1 execute libertas_spatial_fabric –remote \


–file=migrations/0001_spatial_schema.sql


# 3 — Doctrine-compliant preview (default EXECUTION_MODE=DRY_RUN)


npx wrangler deploy –dry-run


# 4 — Verify


curl [https://libertas-location-intelligence.<subdomain&gt](https://libertas-location-intelligence.<subdomain&gt);.workers.dev/health


curl [https://libertas-location-intelligence.<subdomain&gt](https://libertas-location-intelligence.<subdomain&gt);.workers.dev/v1/layers/THEATER-REDSEA-V6/geojson


# ⛔ LIVE cutover (EXECUTION_MODE=LIVE) is gated: requires human_review_id,


# validated-intent header path, and recorded analyst disposition per


# [[Human_Review_Gates]] and [[AEQUITAS_Deterministic_Verification_Layer]].

**Doctrinal Closure**


*The edge serves features, not facts. Every route returns claims with lineage;
the D1 trigger blocks silent promotion; the CHECK constraint blocks control edges;
the Worker defaults to DRY_RUN; and LIVE exists only behind a recorded human gate.*


OBSERVATIONS BECOME FEATURES. FEATURES BECOME RELATIONSHIPS.


RELATIONSHIPS BECOME KNOWLEDGE. KNOWLEDGE REQUIRES PROVENANCE.


THE MAP IS AN EVIDENCE FABRIC — NOW SERVED AT THE EDGE, STILL UNDER REVIEW.


Next options: generate scripts/seed_vectorize.ts (embed seed features into Vectorize), the 11_DASHBOARDS/ full Dataview board, or the 12_VISUALIZATIONS/ 16:9 rendering spec for the edge mesh.

('SOURCE_ASSERTION', 1), ('UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION', 1),  ('CONTESTED', 2), ('ANALYTICAL_INFERENCE', 2), ('PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED', 3),  ('CORROBORATED', 4), ('REVIEWED_ASSESSMENT', 5), ('VERIFIED_FACT', 6),  ('REJECTED', 0), ('SUPERSEDED', 0), ('REFERENCE_METADATA', 0);CREATE TABLE theater_layers (  layer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  name TEXT NOT NULL,  region TEXT NOT NULL,  description FROM epistemic_ranks)),  review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending'    CHECK (review_state IN ('Pending','InReview','Approved','ApprovedWithConditions','Returned','Rejected')),  human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now')));CREATE TABLE geo_features (  feature_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  layer_id TEXT NOT TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now')),  epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNVERIFIED_OBSERVATION'    CHECK (epistemic_status IN (SELECT status FROM epistemic_ranks)),  claim_status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNVERIFIED',  attribution_form TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNRESOLVED',  canonical_digest TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',  review_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',  human_review_required INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1);-- AEQUITAS deterministic verification: block silent epistemic promotion.CREATE TRIGGER trg_no_silent_upgradeBEFORE UPDATE OF epistemic_status ON observationsFOR EACH ROWWHEN (SELECT rank FROM epistemic_ranks WHERE status = NEW.epistemic_status)   > (SELECT rank FROM epistemic_ranks WHERE status = OLD.epistemic_status) AND NOT EXISTS (   SELECT 1 FROM epistemic_transitions t   WHERE t.object_id = OLD.observation_id     AND t.old_epistemic_status = OLD.epistemic_status     AND t.new_epistemic_status = NEW.epistemic_status     AND t.final_disposition IN ('APPROVE','APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS'))BEGIN  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'AEQUITAS_BLOCK: epistemic promotion requires approved transition record');END;CREATE TABLE epistemic_transitions (  transition_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  object_id TEXT NOT NULL,  old_epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL,  new_epistemic_status TEXT NOT NULL,  transition_reason TEXT NOT NULL, ## 3. src/index.ts — Hono Edge Router


```
import { Hono } from 'hono'import { secureHeaders } from 'hono/secure-headers'type Bindings = {  DB: D1Database  THEATER_CACHE: KVNamespace  VECTORIZE: VectorizeIndex  AI: Ai  FRAMEWORK: string  DOCTRINE: string  LOCATION_CONTROLLER: string  EXECUTION_MODE: 'DRY_RUN' | 'LIVE'  CLASSIFICATION: string}const app = new Hono<{ Bindings: Bindings }>()app.use('*', secureHeaders())// ── VERITAS provenance envelope on every response ─────────────────────────app.use('*', async (c, next) => {  await next()  c.header('X-Libertas-Framework', c.env.FRAMEWORK)  c.header('X-Libertas-Execution-Mode', c.env.EXECUTION_MODE)  c.header('X-Libertas-Navigation-Suitability', 'false')  c.header('X-Libertas-Epistemic-Axiom', 'Reports are claims requiring lineage')})// ── Helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────const canonicalize = (v: unknown): string => {  // RFC 8785 (JCS) subset: recursive key sort, no whitespace. Conformance PENDING.  if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object') return JSON.stringify(v)  if (Array.isArray(v)) return '[' + v.map(canonicalize).join(',') + ']'  const o = v as Record<string, unknown>  return '{' + Object.keys(o).sort()    .map(k => JSON.stringify(k) + ':' + canonicalize(o[k])).join(',') + '}'}const sha256Hex = async (s: string): Promise<string> => {  const buf = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(s))  return [...new Uint8Array(buf)].map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('')}const envelope = (c: any, data: unknown, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => ({  data,  provenance: {    framework: c.env.FRAMEWORK,    generated_at: new Date().toISOString(),    navigation_suitability: false,    classification: c.env.CLASSIFICATION,    notices: [      'Conceptual OSINT analytical rendering — not a navigational product.',      'GeoJSON coordinate order is [longitude, latitude].',      'Spatial proximity is not actor attribution.',      'Retrieval rank is not evidence strength.',    ],    ...extra,  },})const rowToFeature = (r: any) => ({  type: 'Feature',  id: r.feature_id,  properties: {    feature_id: r.feature_id, layer_id: r.layer_id, name: r.name,    feature_class: r.feature_class, epistemic_status: r.epistemic_status,    claim_status: r.claim_status, confidence: r.confidence,    attribution_form: r.attribution_form, source_id: r.source_id,    source_locator: r.source_locator, review_state: r.review_state,    human_review_required: !!r.human_review_required,    canonical_digest: r.canonical_digest,    navigation_suitability: false, operational_use: 'PROHIBITED',  },  geometry: JSON.parse(r.geometry_json),})// ── Health ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────app.get('/health', (c) => c.json(envelope(c, {  status: 'CONTEXT_OPERATIONAL',  controller: c.env.LOCATION_CONTROLLER,  doctrine: c.env.DOCTRINE,  execution_mode: c.env.EXECUTION_MODE,})))// ── Layer registry (KV-cached) ─────────────────────────────────────────────app.get('/v1/layers', async (c) => {  const key = 'idx:layers:v1'  const hit = await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.get(key, 'json')  if (hit) return c.json(envelope(c, hit, { cache: 'HIT' }))  const { results } = await c.env.DB.prepare(    `SELECT layer_id, name, region, description, epistemic_status, review_state     FROM theater_layers ORDER BY layer_id`).all()  await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.put(key, JSON.stringify(results), { expirationTtl: 60 })  return c.json(envelope(c, results, { cache: 'MISS' }))})// ── Theater layer as GeoJSON FeatureCollection (KV-cached) ────────────────app.get('/v1/layers/:layerId/geojson', async (c) => {  const layerId = c.req.param('layerId')  const key = `layer:${layerId}:geojson:v1`  const hit = await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.get(key)  if (hit) return c.json(JSON.parse(hit))  const { results } = await c.env.DB.prepare(    `SELECT * FROM geo_features WHERE layer_id = ?1`).bind(layerId).all()  if (!results.length)    return c.json({ error: 'LAYER_NOT_FOUND', layer_id: layerId }, 404)  const fc = {    type: 'FeatureCollection',    name: layerId,    metadata: {      framework: c.env.FRAMEWORK, doctrine: c.env.DOCTRINE,      coordinate_order: '[longitude, latitude]',      navigation_suitability: false,      generated_at: new Date().toISOString(),    },    features: results.map(rowToFeature),  }  await c.env.THEATER_CACHE.put(key, JSON.stringify(fc), { expirationTtl: 30 })  return c.json(fc)})// ── Bounding-box spatial query (indexed) ──────────────────────────────────app.get('/v1/spatial/bbox', async (c) => {  const q = c.req.query()  const nums = ['min_lon', 'min_lat', 'max_lon', 'max_lat'].map(k => Number(q[k]))  if (nums.some(Number.isNaN)) return c.json({ error: 'INVALID_BBOX' }, 400)  const [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] = nums  if (minLon < -180 || maxLon > 180 || minLat < -90 || maxLat > 90)    return c.json({ error: 'BBOX_OUT_OF_RANGE' }, 400)  const { results } = await c.env.DB.prepare(    `SELECT * FROM geo_features     WHERE max_lon >= ?1 AND min_lon <= ?3 AND max_lat >= ?2 AND min_lat <= ?4`)    .bind(minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat).all()  return c.json(envelope(c, {    type: 'FeatureCollection', features: results.map(rowToFeature),  }, { query_bbox: [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat] }))})// ── ORIENT — GraphRAG semantic neighbor search (Vectorize + Workers AI) ────app.get('/v1/orient', async (c) => {  const q = c.req.query('q')  if (!q) return c.json({ error: 'QUERY_REQUIRED' }, 400)  const emb = await c.env.AI.run('@cf/baai/bge-base-en-v1.5', { text: q })  const matches = await c.env.VECTORIZE.query(emb.data[0], {    topK: 5, returnMetadata: 'all',  })  return c.json(envelope(c,    query: q,    semantic_neighbors: match
```


28Deployment controls


Consequential mutations require validated intent and human review.[https://www.linkedin.com/in/jesse-marshall-2613b94b?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afsd_profile%3AACoAAAqPTSkBeQ6WiFBmMkWIndknmbkWgggn0gM](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jesse-marshall-2613b94b?miniProfileUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afsd_profile%3AACoAAAqPTSkBeQ6WiFBmMkWIndknmbkWgggn0gM)


D1 records require `epistemic_status`.


Existing GeoJSON versions are immutable.


Epistemic changes create new versions and transition records.


KV cache objects cannot alter D1 state.


Vector similarity cannot create evidentiary graph edges.


Public API remains read-only.


Conceptual geometry is not navigational.

# Agentic OODA System Architecture

The **Agentic OODA Loop** translates classical decision agility into deterministic, multi-agent orchestration[cite: 7]. The loop shifts from human intuition to **verifiable event provenance, graph state, latent-space orientation, consensus validation, and closed-loop feedback**[cite: 7].
````


┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │ OBSERVE │ ────► │ ORIENT │ ────► │ DECIDE │ │ Event Ingestion │ │ GraphRAG Engine │ │ Consensus Model │ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └────────┬────────┘ ▲ │ │ ┌─────────────────┐ │ └──────────────── │ FEEDBACK │ ◄─────────────┘ │ Lineage Probe │ ACT (Deterministic) └─────────────────┘


```
## Phase-to-Component Mapping

| OODA Phase | Orchestration Component | Core Function | Provenance Requirement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Observe**[cite: 7] | Webhook Listeners, Ingestion Nodes[cite: 7] | Capture telemetry & claims[cite: 7] | Source ID, RFC 8785 JSON, SHA-256 Digest[cite: 7, 8] |
| **Orient**[cite: 7] | GraphRAG Engine, Neo4j, Vector Space[cite: 7] | Contextualize & resolve entities[cite: 7] | Link to prior nodes, policies, & GeoFeatures[cite: 7, 8] |
| **Decide**[cite: 7] | Specialized Multi-Agent Mesh[cite: 7] | Plan generation & risk contest[cite: 7] | Record candidate plans, criticisms, & dissent[cite: 7, 8] |
| **Act**[cite: 7] | API Workers, Allowlisted Tools[cite: 7] | Deterministic plan execution[cite: 7] | Execution ID, Action Hash, Rollback state[cite: 7, 8] |
| **Feedback**[cite: 7] | Probe Agents, State Audit Hooks[cite: 7] | Correlate downstream effects[cite: 7] | Map effects back to originating Execution ID[cite: 7, 8] |

---

## 🚫 Prohibited Implicit Edges


The automated creation of structural control or actor-intent edges is strictly forbidden without verified primary source evidence and human review gates[cite: 8]:


- Prohibited implicit relationships: `CONTROLS`, `DIRECTS`, `OWNS`, `OPERATES_IN`, `TARGETS`, `COMMANDS`[cite: 8].


## 🔍 Retrieval Strategy


1. **Vector Space Query:** Retrieve top-k semantic chunks based on embedding similarity[cite: 7].
2. **Graph Expansion:** Traverse explicit Neo4j edges to fetch associated `GeoFeature`, `Digest`, and `EvidenceChain` nodes[cite: 7, 8].
3. **Policy-As-Code Check:** Filter retrieved graph context against active governance constraints before passing to the decision mesh[cite: 7, 8].

# Multi-Agent Consensus Model

Decision formulation is structured as an explicit, adversarial contest among specialized sub-agents to prevent hallucinated or unauthorized actions[cite: 7].
````


[ Structured Context ] │ ▼ Proposer Agent ──► Generates Candidate Plan │ ▼ Critic Agent ──► Identifies Gaps & Cascade Risks │ ▼ Policy Agent ──► Validates Scope (NIST 800-53 / FedRAMP) │ ▼ Provenance Agent ──► Validates Unbroken Lineage & Digests │ ▼ Consensus Engine ──► Evaluates Agreement & Score │ ▼ [ Human Interrupt ] ──► Final Analyst Clearance


```
## Specialized Agent Roles

* **Proposer Agent:** Formulates candidate remediation or analytical plans[cite: 7].
* **Critic Agent:** Identifies hidden assumptions, risks, and failure modes[cite: 7].
* **Policy Agent:** Enforces regulatory and scope boundaries[cite: 7].
* **Security Agent:** Verifies access conditions and injection safeguards[cite: 7].
* **Provenance Agent:** Validates complete source attribution and RFC 8785 hashes[cite: 7, 8].
* **Human Review Agent:** Manages the interrupt hook for high-risk decisions[cite: 7].
```

---title: Cryptographic Provenance Fabricartifact: CRYPTO_PROVENANCE_FABRIC_v6_10type: provenance-specframework: LIBERTAS_v6.10primitives: FIPS 180-2 SHA-256, ML-KEM-1024, ML-DSA-87compliance: NIST 800-53 Rev5 / FedRAMP Moderate+ / EO 14413epistemic_status: REVIEWED_ASSESSMENTclassification: UNCLASSIFIED // OSINTtags: [Provenance, PostQuantum, Cryptography, RFC8785, AuditTrail]---# Cryptographic Provenance FabricThe provenance fabric guarantees that every knowledge object inside the **American Science Cloud (AmSC)** possesses an immutable, mathematically verifiable lineage[cite: 2, 8].## 🔐 Cryptographic Primitive Stack1. **Canonicalization (RFC 8785):** Enforces deterministic, byte-level JSON formatting by removing whitespace variance and standardizing key ordering[cite: 2, 7, 8].2. **Digest Hashing (FIPS 180-2 SHA-256):** Computes a unique, tamper-proof fingerprint for every canonical payload[cite: 2, 4, 8].3. **Key Encapsulation (ML-KEM / Kyber-1024):** Post-quantum cryptographic encapsulation securing inter-agent communication channels[cite: 2, 8].4. **Digital Signatures (ML-DSA / Dilithium-87):** Post-quantum digital signatures validating agent attestation and review sign-offs[cite: 2, 8].

Architectural separation of concerns## LIBERTAS — Knowledge architectureLIBERTAS defines how analytical knowledge is organized, linked, retrieved, rendered,versioned, and inspected.Responsibilities include:- Open and composable data structures- Obsidian-compatible knowledge organization- GraphRAG retrieval- GeoJSON spatial representation- Explicit node and relationship schemas- Reversible transformations- Interoperable analytical workflows- Human-readable and machine-readable artifactsLIBERTAS does not determine whether a claim is true.## VERITAS — Evidence and provenanceVERITAS preserves the evidentiary context of every material knowledge object.Mandatory concerns include:- Source attribution- Source locators- Canonicalization records- Content digests- Evidence lineage- Transformation history- Source-dependence analysis- Supporting and contradicting evidence- Uncertainty- Reproducibility- Epistemic statusVERITAS does not authorize consequential execution.## AEQUITAS — Deterministic verification and governanceAEQUITAS applies deterministic controls to proposed state changes and executionrequests.Responsibilities include:- Schema validation- Mandatory-field enforcement- Silent-upgrade detection- Policy-as-code checks- Security gates- Scope validation- Human-review routing- Rollback validation- Dissent preservation- Audit-record generationAEQUITAS verification must fail closed when a mandatory field, source reference,authorization, or review record is missing.## Separation rule```textLIBERTAS organizes knowledge.VERITAS preserves why it may be believed.AEQUITAS governs whether it may advance or execute.```No component may silently assume the authority of another.---# 2. Architectural invariants1. Every material observation begins as a claim or unverified observation.2. Every claim-bearing object has an `epistemic_status`.3. Retrieval rank is not evidence strength.4. Semantic similarity is not corroboration.5. Spatial proximity is not actor attribution.6. Repeated dependent reporting is not independent corroboration.7. Model confidence is not evidence confidence.8. Expert agreement is not a substitute for evidence.9. Graph edges require evidence identifiers.10. Missing output is not approval.11. Mandatory gate failures cannot be averaged away.12. Consequential epistemic promotions require explicit transition records.13. Only allowlisted deterministic components may execute.14. Every execution has an execution identifier, action hash, and rollback state.15. Every effect returns to observation with its originating execution identifier.16. Prior versions remain immutable and traceable.17. Hidden reasoning is not stored; concise decision summaries are retained.18. Human-review requirements combine using logical `OR`.19. The most restrictive applicable constraint governs.20. No conceptual map is treated as a navigational or operational product.---# 3.
